subject.title: Feature: Add denylist support for exec-approvals

question: Should native exec approvals adopt the linked PR’s deny-over-allow overlay, and should a match force human-only one-shot approval or support a separate hard-deny action?
rationale: This determines a persisted, cross-host security-policy contract and the meaning of future approval decisions; implementation mechanics cannot safely choose those semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Human-only deny overlay
options.body: Add deny patterns that take precedence over broad allow decisions, force an explicit one-shot human approval, and prevent matched commands from creating durable trust.

options.title: Allow prompt and hard-deny actions
options.body: Extend each rule with an explicit action so operators can choose human approval or unconditional denial, accepting a larger policy and UI surface.

options.title: Keep core allowlist-only
options.body: Decline native deny rules and document external policy plugins such as CRE or SafeClaw for operators who accept a trusted-plugin enforcement layer.

recommendation.title: Human-only deny overlay
recommendation.body: Add deny patterns that take precedence over broad allow decisions, force an explicit one-shot human approval, and prevent matched commands from creating durable trust.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor has the strongest combined product-authority, issue-discussion, and current implementation-history signals for the security-policy choice.
